title: Dubu Jorim Braised Tofu
shortDescription: Firm tofu is pan-fried until golden, then briefly braised in a savory soy, garlic, scallion, and gochugaru sauce.
culturalContext: Dubu jorim is a Korean tofu side dish in the jorim family of seasoned braises. Seasoning balance, aromatics, chile level, and whether the tofu is fried first vary by household.
author: {{LEGAL_NAME}}
equipment: Nonstick or well-seasoned skillet with lid
Paper towels or clean kitchen towel

ingredients.preparation: drained and cut into 1 cm / 3/8-inch slabs

instructions.heading: Drain and dry
instructions.action: Drain the tofu, cut it into even slabs, and blot every surface dry.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: The tofu surfaces feel dry and the slabs remain intact.
instructions.safetyNote: Drying limits splatter when tofu meets hot oil.

instructions.heading: Mix the sauce
instructions.action: Combine soy sauce, water, gochugaru, garlic, half the scallions, sesame oil, and sesame seeds in a clean bowl.
instructions.safetyNote: Check soy sauce labels for wheat/gluten and sesame declarations.

instructions.heading: Brown the first side
instructions.action: Heat oil over medium heat, add tofu in one layer, and cook without moving until golden underneath.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: The underside is evenly golden and releases from the pan.
instructions.safetyNote: Lower tofu away from you and protect exposed skin from hot-oil splatter.

instructions.heading: Turn and brown
instructions.action: Turn with a thin spatula and brown the second side.
instructions.safetyNote: Turn gently to avoid splashing hot oil.

instructions.heading: Braise briefly
instructions.action: Pour sauce around the tofu, cover partly, and simmer until the sauce reduces, spooning it over the slabs once.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: The tofu is steaming and a small amount of sauce clings to it.
instructions.safetyNote: Open the lid away from your face.

instructions.heading: Finish and store
instructions.action: Top with remaining scallions, rest 5 minutes, and transfer to a clean dish.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: The sauce has settled into a glossy coating.
instructions.safetyNote: Refrigerate within 2 hours in a shallow covered container.

grillSetup: Not applicable; this banchan is pan-fried and braised on the stovetop.
visualDonenessCues: Sauce is reduced but not dry
Tofu is hot and steaming throughout
foodSafetyNotes: Blot tofu dry before adding it to hot oil to reduce splatter.
Use separate clean utensils and serving ware after cooking.
Refrigerate within 2 hours at or below 40°F / 4°C.
Declare soy, wheat/gluten, and sesame allergens.

allergens.crossContactWarning: Contains soy, wheat/gluten, and sesame; verify labels and prevent cross-contact for any adaptation.

substitutions: Use certified gluten-free tamari only after verifying every label.
Use a milder quantity of gochugaru to reduce heat.
ingredientSourcing: Choose firm tofu that is cold, sealed, and within its use-by date.
Buy Korean gochugaru from a high-turnover market and refrigerate after opening.
makeAhead: Mix the sauce up to 1 day ahead and refrigerate; cook the tofu close to serving.
storage: Cool promptly, refrigerate in a covered shallow container within 2 hours, and use within 4 days pending food-safety approval.
reheating: Reheat gently in a covered skillet with a spoonful of water until steaming throughout.
leftovers: Serve properly refrigerated leftovers with hot rice within the approved storage window.
servingSuggestions: Serve warm or cool with rice and other banchan.

faq.question: Do I need to press the tofu?
faq.answer: A brief drain and thorough surface drying are sufficient for this draft; test cooking must confirm texture.

faq.question: Can I omit gochugaru?
faq.answer: Yes, but the flavor profile will be milder.
